How deficit-framed is a set of results?

Source: R/indigenous_frameworks.R
frmaud.Rd

Counts how many of the indicators in a report measure distress, deficit or disparity and how many measure wellness or strength, and names any group reported on deficits alone.

Usage

frmaud(x)

Arguments

x

A welprof.

Value

A list of class rmbl_framing: bygrp (a data frame of group, wellness, distress, shrdef), shrdef overall and defonly (the groups with no wellness indicator).

Details

Walter (2016) shows that statistics about Indigenous peoples cluster around five Ds: disparity, deprivation, disadvantage, dysfunction and difference. Results built only of those describe Indigenous peoples as their problems. This audit does not measure anything about people; it measures the report: the share of its indicators that are deficit-framed, overall and per group, so a report can be balanced before it is published. Pair each gap with a strength-framed level (welprof, dualcont).

References

Walter M (2016). Data politics and Indigenous representation in Australian statistics. In Kukutai T, Taylor J (eds), Indigenous Data Sovereignty: Toward an Agenda, 79-97. ANU Press. doi:10.22459/caepr38.11.2016.05

Walter M, Andersen C (2013). Indigenous Statistics: A Quantitative Research Methodology. Left Coast Press. doi:10.4324/9781315426570

Examples

wb <- indiex("wellbeing")
w <- welprof(wb, "group", "indicator", "estimate", "lower", "upper",
                      well = "Always or often has a hopeful outlook",
                      distress = c("Rarely or never has a hopeful outlook",
                                   "Life satisfaction rating between 0 and 5",
                                   "Fair or poor perceived health"))
frmaud(w)
#> 75% of the indicators reported are deficit-framed.
#> Most of this report measures disparity or deficit; pair each with a strength-framed level.
